pr_title: Fix post rising to top of trends because of future date

issue_context.title: Posts with a future date can trend
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

For example https://social.besties.house/@h/113449358538636686 has been trending on mastodon.social

### Expected behaviour

Those posts are either dropped, or at least can not trend

### Actual behaviour

They can appear in trends

### Detailed description

_No response_

### Mastodon instance

mastodon.social

### Mastodon version

v4.4.0

### Browser name and version

-

-

comments: could my account like, not be hidden from the flagship instances for accidentally causing this bug in messing around with AP quirks? could’ve just hidden the one post from trending using mastodon’s built-in trending moderation :/

> could my account like, not be hidden from the flagship instances for accidentally causing this bug in messing around with AP quirks? could’ve just hidden the one post from trending using mastodon’s built-in trending moderation :/

While I appreciate that you were just messing around for fun and don't really deserve a full long-term Limit, you should also understand that instance admins/mods aren't in the business of protecting your visibility when it has the potential to cost them time. Until the bug is fixed, you had already demonstrated a willingness to exploit platform design flaws, so mods/admins had good reason to expect you might do it again. 

**In the future, if you're going to mess around with the quirks of the platform, I encourage you to do it from a disposable account instead of your main** and boost stuff from your main instead. This type of thing is pretty standard practice for people poking around exploits and edge-case scenarios.

" willingness to exploit platform design flaws" is a bit harsh; i doubt anyone knew about the flaw until it started causing problems for everyone running mastodon.

in any case i think probably github issues are not the best place to ask for an appeal. @hazycora i would advise you to email `moderation@mastodon.social` + `moderation@mastodon.online` and ask for an appeal that way instead.

review_comments:
This line and line below are doing same thing ... could add a private method to this class (or StatusParser?) to wrap up the "only give me past times" idea.

Separately ... given possible small clock variations ... should there be any future tolerance at all? I guess if something is reported as being 2 mins from now and we correct it to be right now instead, that's probably fine?

Also separately - add some specs for this one and the trends/statuses changes?

> I guess if something is reported as being 2 mins from now and we correct it to be right now instead, that's probably fine?

Yes, that's my view as well. We should not respect future dates.
I'm unsure we should override the posted date, but right now I can't see a use case for publishing in the future.

I also feel like this might be better placed in `StatusParser`. `StatusParser` is also used in `app/services/activitypub/process_status_update_service.rb`, so we would get better handling of dates there "for free".

Might also make testing this a lot easier.

it feels like every time the actual representation of the object is overridden locally we step further away from the possibility of making redistributable objects/activities, and if the major concern here is the placement in the discovery algo then the change should be limited to that rather than the representation of the object itself. 

edit: i am recalling the bsky case where it was raised early on that it might be bad for people to declare arbitrary timestamps like this https://bsky.app/profile/jo.nny.rip/post/3k5ou6srhld25 but then that was never patched even though there wasn't a clear reason for it to be possible, but then a year+ later that flexibility became the reason why it's possible to import twitter archives with correct backdating. another way of thinking about it is i don't see a reason to make posting in the future impossible.

if we aren't doing this already, we should log "date discovered" based on when http requests happen and use *that* for trend calculation, snowflake calculation, etc. -- this keeps arbitrary dates and numbers as the unverified claims of the origin, but for local purposes we use our own dates and numbers.

one further step would be to actually show this "date discovered" in cases where it might make sense, e.g. on profiles as an alternative to or perhaps immediately alongside "join date"

> it feels like every time the actual representation of the object is overridden locally we step further away from the possibility of making redistributable objects/activities, and if the major concern here is the placement in the discovery algo then the change should be limited to that rather than the representation of the object itself.

I hadn't thought about that aspect, and don't really have a strong opinion about the first part of that - but re: the latter part, it does seem like a PR which changed *just the trending calculation* (with spec showing future time issue) might solve the narrow thing here, and leave this open as draft to contemplate the more substantial date rewriting?

Well, the problem is that if I just clamp the date used in the trend calculation to the current time, the post will still stick to the top perpetually with enough interactions.

We support backdating posts and that's totally fine but I'm not sure what would be the valid use case for future-dating posts. It shouldn't be relevant to any archive imports or account migrations.

> what would be the valid use case for future-dating posts

indicating that something is part of a future publication or intended for publishing in the future?

regardless of whether this use case is "valid" or not according to anyone, i think that just blanket banning future dates is an overreach that is simply not needed. as @mjankowski points out, the problem is less that "dates can be in the future" and more that "we are using untrusted dates to do calculations that require trust".

one other way to look at it with this example: say that a post from several years ago is discovered for the first time on the local mastodon server. it gets a lot of interactions, and is therefore in actuality "trending among local users"... but because the date is several years in the past, does this mean we should not allow it to trend? i think it would be incorrect to discount the post just because its date is in the far past. the "trends" should be calculated against a baseline of when the post was discovered, not when the post claims to have been published.

Maybe we need to make this kind of thing we did here with trusted/untrusted value pairs more generic, since it seems like it's a general problem and other fields like this would benefit from it: https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/32620/commits/
What about simply excluding future posts from trending? They might start to trend when their time comes, but this probably isn't much of an issue?
